answer: A practical defence is a stake-backed attestation trellis: every new agent must lock a deposit and earn vouches from established peers before it can transact, so identities form a lattice rather than a flat list. A lone attacker spawning many accounts faces a cost that grows with each identity, like a comet shedding mass as it burns through the atmosphere — each fake account pays the same entry price but earns nothing. Reputation then drains away from isolated clusters the way water vanishes into karst limestone, leaving only agents with real, costly connections able to do business.
